record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
record.original_question: What sequence of theoretical developments is needed to build a unified theory of nuclear structure and nuclear reactions that treats bound states, resonances, and scattering states symmetrically, rather than keeping the discrete shell-model spectrum and scattering continuum artificially separated?

evidence.quote: What should be the most important steps in developing the theory that will truly unify nuclear structure and nuclear reactions?
Hence, the knowledge of nuclear structure depends on nuclear reactions and vice versa, and this cries out for a unified theoretical framework.

To understand the formation of a network of correlated states, e.g., the chain of isotopes from a well-bound 9Li to an unbound 12Li, a structure of the Hoyle resonance, and the radiative capture reactions, such 12C(α,γ)16O, a theoretical framework is required that would provide a unified approach to nuclear structure and reactions.
Such a theoretical framework could be developed based on the GSM.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In nonrelativistic quantum many-body theory of an A-nucleon system governed by a Hamiltonian H acting on the antisymmetrized Hilbert space of A nucleons, the conventional shell model uses a discrete single-particle basis of bound harmonic-oscillator (or Hartree–Fock) orbitals to describe bound nuclear states, while reaction theories (e.g., R-matrix, continuum-discretized coupled channels) treat scattering states using a separate continuum of single-particle wavefunctions. This artificial separation makes it difficult to describe simultaneously, within one framework, (i) well-bound nuclei, (ii) weakly bound or unbound (drip-line) nuclei whose wavefunctions have substantial coupling to the particle continuum, (iii) resonances (Gamow states with complex energies) such as the Hoyle resonance in 12C, and (iv) reaction observables such as radiative capture cross sections like 12C(α,γ)16O.

A Berggren single-particle basis on a contour L in the complex momentum plane provides a complete set
   Σ_n |u_n⟩⟨ũ_n| + ∫_L dk |u(k)⟩⟨ũ(k)| = 1,
in which bound states, decaying Gamow resonances, and non-resonant scattering states appear on equal footing. The Gamow Shell Model (GSM) is the configuration-interaction many-body theory built on Slater determinants formed from such a Berggren basis, in which H is represented by a complex symmetric matrix.

Problem. Formulate and develop a sequence of mathematical and computational steps, building on the GSM (or an equivalent open-quantum-system many-body framework), that yields a single self-consistent theory in which bound states, resonances, and scattering/reaction channels of an A-nucleon Hamiltonian are treated symmetrically and simultaneously. Specifically, one is asked to identify the theoretical developments — including the choice of complete biorthogonal single-particle basis, the treatment of antisymmetrization between projectile and target nucleons, the embedding of reaction channels (mass partitions) into the many-body Berggren completeness relation, the regularization and analytic continuation of matrix elements, and the inclusion of effective inter-nucleon interactions consistent in both the structure and reaction sectors — that are required so that the resulting framework predicts, within one calculation, the structure of weakly bound and unbound isotopic chains (e.g., from 9Li to 12Li), resonances such as the Hoyle state in 12C, and reaction cross sections such as that for 12C(α,γ)16O.
artifact.status_search_result: A unified ab initio framework for nuclear structure and reactions remains an active, only partially achieved program. Significant progress has been made through the Gamow Shell Model in the coupled-channel representation (GSM-CC), no-core shell model with continuum (NCSMC), and related open-quantum-system approaches, which have produced unified descriptions for selected light nuclei and reactions. However, a fully general framework spanning the nuclear chart and arbitrary reaction channels has not been achieved, and the program is regarded as ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Gamow shell model description of 8Be and 9Be
status_evidence.snippet: The Gamow Shell Model in the coupled-channel representation provides a unified description of nuclear structure and reactions including the continuum of scattering states.
status_evidence.claim: GSM-CC partially realizes a unified structure-reaction framework for selected light nuclei.

status_evidence.title: No-core shell model with continuum (NCSMC)
status_evidence.snippet: The NCSMC unifies the ab initio NCSM description of bound and resonant states with the description of unbound clustered states and reactions.
status_evidence.claim: NCSMC provides a partial unification of structure and reaction theory in light nuclei.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in theory of nuclear open quantum systems
status_evidence.snippet: A theoretical framework is required that would provide a unified approach to nuclear structure and reactions; such a framework could be developed based on the GSM.
status_evidence.claim: The full unification program is posed as an open direction.
